hero.title: Union Executive: President
hero.description: Master the constitutional office of the President of India (Articles 52 to 62, 72, 111, 123, 143)—including election methods, impeachment procedure, powers and functions, veto mechanisms, pardoning powers, and the ordinance-making power (UPSC GS Paper-II: Indian Polity).

mockIntro.title: Interactive UPSC Mock Test
mockIntro.description: Evaluate your understanding of Articles 52-62, presidential election math, impeachment, pardoning powers, ordinances, and vetoes through a timed test.

timeline.title: Key Milestones & Constitutional Cases
timeline.description: Important historical events and landmark judicial pronouncements concerning the office of the President.

cards.details: The Supreme Court ruled that the President is only a formal, constitutional head who must act on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers, with rare exceptions.
The 42nd Amendment made PM's advice binding. The 44th Amendment allowed the President to return advice once for reconsideration, but the reconsidered advice is binding.

cards.period: D.C. Wadhwa v. State of Bihar
cards.details: The Supreme Court held that the repromulgation of ordinances without attempting to pass them in the legislature is a subversion of the democratic process and unconstitutional.

cards.period: Epu Sudhakar v. Govt. of AP
cards.details: The Supreme Court held that the pardoning power of the President/Governor under Articles 72/161 is subject to judicial review to check for arbitrariness, bias, or mala fide intent.

mnemonics.title: Mnemonics & Memory Hacks
mnemonics.description: Quick memory hooks to retain Article ranges and pardoning classifications.

items.title: Mnemonic 1
items.decryption: Sequential scope of articles: President of India (Art 52), Executive power (Art 53), Method of election (Art 54 & 55), Term of office (Art 56), Qualifications (Art 58), Oath or affirmation (Art 60), Impeachment procedure (Art 61).

items.title: Mnemonic 2
items.decryption: Five pardoning powers: Commutation (lighter form), Remission (reduced duration), Respite (special conditions), Reprieve (temporary stay), Pardon (complete absolution).

items.title: Mnemonic 3
items.decryption: Remember that Article 123 is the Ordinance-making power of the President, which has the force of an Act of Parliament but is temporary.

flashcards.title: Active Recall Flashcards
flashcards.description: Active-recall review of presidential powers and election process.

items.question: Who are the members of the Electoral College that elects the President of India?
items.answer: Elected members only: (1) Both Houses of Parliament, (2) Legislative Assemblies of all States, and (3) Legislative Assemblies of Delhi, Puducherry, and Jammu & Kashmir. Nominated members do not vote.

items.question: Are nominated members of Parliament allowed to participate in the impeachment of the President?
items.answer: Yes. Nominated members of Parliament do participate in the impeachment of the President under Article 61, even though they do not vote in his election.

items.question: Does the President of India have the power of a qualified veto?
items.answer: No. Unlike the US President who possesses a qualified veto (which can be overridden by a higher majority in the legislature), the Indian President possesses only Absolute, Suspensive, and Pocket vetoes.

items.question: What is the maximum life of an ordinance promulgated by the President under Article 123?
items.answer: 6 months and 6 weeks. An ordinance must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks of its reassembly. Since the maximum gap between two sessions of Parliament is 6 months, the maximum life is 6 months + 6 weeks.

items.question: Can the President pardon a death sentence under Article 72?
items.answer: Yes. The President has the exclusive power to pardon a death sentence. The Governor under Article 161 can suspend, remit, or commute a death sentence, but cannot pardon it.

traps.title: UPSC Civil Services Exam Traps to Avoid
items: Trap 1: Believing nominated members of State Assemblies vote in the election or impeachment. State assembly nominated members do not vote in the election, and state assembly members (elected or nominated) do not participate in the impeachment process at all (impeachment is done entirely by Parliament).

Trap 2: Assuming the President can return a Money Bill for reconsideration. No! The President can either give assent or withhold assent to a Money Bill, but cannot return it for reconsideration (under Article 111).

Trap 3: Confusing the majority required for impeachment. It requires a majority of not less than two-thirds of the total membership of the House (not present and voting) in both houses, making it the most stringent majority in the Constitution.

sections.title: 1. Election, Qualifications & Impeachment
sections.content:
Electoral System (Articles 54 & 55)

The President is elected indirectly by an Electoral College consisting of: (1) Elected members of both Houses of Parliament, (2) Elected members of State Legislative Assemblies, and (3) Elected members of Delhi and Puducherry Assemblies (added by the 70th Amendment Act, 1992). The voting is by secret ballot using proportional representation with a single transferable vote. The value of an MLA's vote is determined by state population divided by total elected MLAs, divided by 1000. MP vote value is total MLA vote value divided by total elected MPs.

Impeachment Particulars:

  • Ground: 'Violation of the Constitution' (not defined in the Constitution).
  • Initiation: Charge signed by 1/4th members of the initiating house.
  • Notice: 14 days written notice must be delivered to the President.
  • Passage: Requires a special majority of two-thirds of the total membership of the house (both houses separately).

sections.title: 2. Powers, Functions & Veto Mechanisms
sections.content:
Veto Powers under Article 111

When a bill passed by Parliament is presented to the President, he has three options: (1) Give assent, (2) Withhold assent (Absolute Veto), or (3) Return the bill for reconsideration (Suspensive Veto). If the bill is passed again by Parliament (with or without amendment) by a simple majority, the President must assent. The President can also take no action (Pocket Veto) since the Constitution doesn't define a timeline.

Power CategoryKey Constitutional Functions
Executive PowersAll executive actions taken in his name. Appoints PM, Ministers, Attorney General, CAG, UPSC, and Governors.
Legislative PowersSummons/prorogues Parliament, addresses joint sessions, dissolves Lok Sabha, nominates 12 Rajya Sabha members.
Judicial PowersAppoints Chief Justice and judges of Supreme Court and High Courts. Seeks advisory opinion from Supreme Court (Art 143).

sections.title: 3. Pardoning (Art 72) & Ordinance-Making (Art 123)
sections.content:
Pardoning Power (Article 72)

The President can grant pardons, reprieves, respites or remissions of punishment or suspend, remit or commute sentences of any person convicted of any offense: (a) in all cases where the punishment is by a Court Martial, (b) where the offense is against a Union law, and (c) in all cases where the sentence is a sentence of death.

Ordinance-Making Power (Article 123)

Parliament's recess power: Promulgated when both houses are not in session, and President is satisfied that immediate action is necessary. An ordinance has the same force as an act of Parliament. It must be approved by Parliament within 6 weeks of its reassembly, otherwise, it ceases to operate. Maximum life is 6 months and 6 weeks.

Five Forms of Pardoning Power:

  • Pardon: Removes both the conviction and sentence, completely absolving the offender.
  • Commutation: Substitutes one form of punishment for a lighter form (e.g., death sentence to rigorous imprisonment).
  • Remission: Reduces the period of sentence without changing its character (e.g., rigorous imprisonment for 2 years reduced to 1 year).
  • Respite: Awards a lesser sentence in place of one originally awarded due to some special fact (e.g., pregnancy of a woman offender).
  • Reprieve: Stays the execution of a sentence (especially death sentence) for a temporary period to enable the offender to seek pardon.
